source.title: Minimum Time to Revert Word to Initial State I

teaching.hint: Which characters after several operations are still forced by the original word?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: Before all original characters are removed, the remaining original suffix is forced at the front; all later characters can be chosen freely.
solution_outline.approach: Test positive times t with t*k below the word length. Restoration is possible exactly when the surviving suffix equals the original prefix of the same length. Return the first passing time; otherwise use ceil(n/k), when no original character remains.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: At time t with t*k<n, the front n-t*k characters are exactly the original suffix starting at t*k. The remaining t*k positions are freely supplied append choices.
solution_outline.correctness: The forced suffix must match the desired original prefix, making the test necessary. When it does, append the required remaining suffix in k-character blocks, making restoration achievable. Once all original characters have left, choose all surviving appended characters to form the original. Testing times in order gives the least positive feasible one.
solution_outline.complexity: `O(n^2/k)` time for direct comparisons and `O(1)` auxiliary space.
solution_outline.pitfall: The operation permits new characters, so treating it as a cyclic rotation imposes a constraint absent from the task.

source_fidelity_notes: Retained freely chosen append characters, mandatory two-part operations, positive-time objective, and small limits.
Omitted the canonical unfinished KMP alternative; used its complete direct suffix/prefix characterization.
common_wrong_turns: The operation permits new characters, so treating it as a cyclic rotation imposes a constraint absent from the task.
